COPE reported that the 6-acre UDA land was leased for 99 years in 2019 without Board approval, and that additional conditions not approved by the Board were included in the lease agreement.
COPE reported a government loss of Rs. 330 million from leasing UDA land bordering D. R. Wijewardena Mawatha without formal Board approval.

Audit reported that land enjoyment was transferred in 2003 outside the normal leasing procedure, later passed to another company without Commission approval; arrears, a released surcharge, and a questionable reduction in assessed lease value were also recorded.

Audit found that lease agreements had not been signed for land leased to four institutions, lease receivables from 2008 had not been collected, and the receivable could not be computed without agreements.

Audit reported that multiple land plots had been used by a company without any amount recovered from Rs. 32,475,109 in lease rent due as at 31 December 2022, and no lease agreement had been entered into.
Audit reported that 10 acres approved for tea cultivation had no lease rent paid since 2011, no formal agreement, and Rs. 1,824,000 outstanding as at the end of 2022.
Audit reported that a private party had informally used leased land from 2008 without approval, agreement or payment, with Rs. 18,403,926 recorded as rent due through 2023.
Audit reported Rs. 5.59 million in lease rent receivable 13 years after a lease for a rocky land plot, with the intended activity not completed and enforcement action delayed.
Audit reported that a 30-year residential lease granted in June 2012 had received no lease payments after 11 years, with Rs. 216,960 due.
Audit reported that a commercial lease running from 2004 had accumulated Rs. 1,069,140 in unpaid lease amounts through 31 December 2023.

A UDA land parcel approved for a 99-year mixed-development lease was later set for a fresh procurement process after the selected investor failed to meet transfer conditions and the earlier lease process was cancelled.

The Otters Aquatic Club occupied government land in Colombo 07 under a lease that expired, while lease arrears of about Rs. 31 million were reported. The Divisional Secretary issued eviction/vacate directions after the arrears were not fully settled and the lease was not renewed.

The Government took over the land and building occupied by the 80 Club at Independence Avenue, Colombo 07 after reported violations including non-payment of lease arrears. The Thimbirigasyaya Divisional Secretary stated that the property was government-owned and was taken back in November 2020.

Public reporting documented allegations that government forest land in the Wandama–Demaliya–Kuda Oya area was leased by an official attached to the Buttala Divisional Secretariat to companies and businessmen despite the land's forest/protected character, prompting government and parliamentary scrutiny.

The Auditor General reported that Sri Lanka Railways owns the land rights of nine CPSTL sub-depots. The lease agreement for those lands expired on 31 December 2013, but CPSTL continued using them without renewing the agreement or entering into a new lease agreement.

The Auditor General reported that SLTDA had received 2,056.73 acres across 12 Kalpitiya islands as free grants for tourism, of which 668.69 acres in 10 islands had been leased to seven companies during 2010, 2011, 2020 and 2022; none of those companies had commenced operations by the end of the audit period.

The Auditor General reported that 510.086 acres at Kuchchaveli had been taken over for tourism development. By 2020–2021, three companies had received leases totaling 49 acres, but only one of those three was operating by the end of the audit period; additional lease agreements and approvals were also in progress.

The Auditor General reported that the Transworks Square land in Colombo Fort was leased to a locally incorporated foreign private company through four agreements between 2013 and 2016 for Rs. 4,999.7 million for a mixed-development project. The project was expected to be completed by 2021, but by the end of 2024 only the structural framework for 60 of the planned 81 floors had been completed. An expected Rs. 1,290.04 million difference between the lease value and market value had not been recovered because the development project remained suspended.

The Auditor General reported that land at Pitipana, Homagama was acquired on a thirty-year lease on 30 April 2014 for Rs. 4.08 million after UDA approval for a rehabilitation and treatment centre. The land had not been used for the approved purpose and remained idle for ten years, while action was still being taken to obtain the indenture of lease.

The Auditor General reported that the Board of Investment allocated an 8-by-8-foot space from the service area next to the Kandy Industrial Park office building for a Bank of Ceylon generator room without entering into an agreement. As a result, rent had not been determined or charged for the allocated space.

The Auditor General reported that the Board of Investment leased 16 acres in the Katunayake Export Processing Zone to the Free Trade Zone Sports Association under an agreement dated 27 September 1988. The rent remained Rs. 200 per acre per year until September 2018, and the Board proposed an increase to Rs. 1,000 per acre for 30 years without obtaining an independent valuer's report. The Board had also spent Rs. 2.5 million to rehabilitate the ground while earning only Rs. 16,000 per year from the land.

The Auditor General reported that a Battaramulla land parcel provided for the Water Resources Board had an annual government-assessed rent of Rs. 2.7 million, but a formal lease agreement with the Urban Development Authority had still not been signed. The Board had paid about Rs. 27.97 million in rent from 2016 to the end of 2024 and had sub-leased the land to the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment from August 2023 at a monthly rent of Rs. 460,000.

The Auditor General reported that the Chamber of Construction Industry obtained 30 perches of land from the Urban Development Authority under a 30-year lease agreement signed on 29 December 2021 at an annual rent of Rs. 1.68 million. The lease required a new secretariat building to be constructed within two years, but construction had not commenced by 31 May 2023.

The Auditor General reported that Waters Edge earned Rs. 10,719,033 in annual rent from LALA Park, but a lease agreement for the underlying land had not been signed with the lessor. Management stated that the arrangement was being negotiated with the parent company, the Urban Development Authority, to execute the land lease.

The Auditor General reported that 100 acres of government land in the Kusala Grama Niladhari Division of Arachchikattu had been leased to a private company under a long-term lease. The lease was cancelled in January 2004 because payments had been in default since 1997, but lease arrears and penalty interest calculated at Rs. 36,587,033 up to May 2013 had still not been recovered.

The Auditor General reported that about 29 acres and 10 perches of government land in the Manativ Grama Niladhari Division of the Puttalam Divisional Secretariat had been leased to a private company for 30 years from 29 June 1988. The company later sold the leased land to another private company on 11 June 2008 without approval from the Provincial Land Commissioner.

The Auditor General reported that approximately 20.234 hectares of government land in the Manativ Grama Niladhari Division of the Puttalam Divisional Secretariat had been leased to a private company for 30 years from 24 February 1993. Lease arrears remained outstanding during the lease period, and when the agreement ended in February 2023, arrears and penalties due from the company had not been fully recovered.

The Auditor General reported that government land provided by the Akuressa Divisional Secretariat to the Akuressa Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society under long-term lease No. L/2940 had been leased until 11 January 1995. After the lease ended, the land continued to be occupied without a long-term lease agreement and without paying rent for about 26 years. Long-term rent due for 1995 to 2009 alone was reported as Rs. 5.23 million.

The Auditor General reported that 0.238 hectares of government land in the Gangawata Korale Divisional Secretariat Division, Kandy, was granted to a private company on a 30-year long-term lease in 2006 for a resort. The same lessee had occupied the land unlawfully from 1995 to 2006, and the Government Valuer assessed lost revenue of Rs. 6,932,500 for that period.

The Auditor General reported that 29.88 perches of government land in the Thimbirigasyaya Divisional Secretariat Division had been given to Independent Television Network Limited on long-term lease in 1999. Notification of the payable lease amount was delayed by nearly three years and no rent was levied for ten years; Rs. 36,225,000 remained due, while the absence of an issued lease prevented legal action for non-payment.

The Auditor General reported that 2 acres, 1 rood and 10 perches of land in the Dodangoda Divisional Secretariat area had been leased to a private institution for 30 years. An outstanding lease amount of Rs. 254,100 remained at the end of 2015.

The Auditor General reported that land on Highlevel Road, Nugegoda, belonging to the Dehiwala Divisional Secretariat had been leased for 30 years in 2000. The lease required rent to be reassessed every five years by at least 50 percent, but revisions were not made in 2005 or 2010, and Rs. 1,342,234 remained outstanding by October 2015.

The Auditor General reported that 4.209 hectares of land at Thalagolla Village, Ragama, had been leased to Colombo North Medical College for 30 years in 1981 and was later used by the Medical Faculty of the University of Kelaniya. The lease expired in May 2011, but the agreement was not extended, causing about four and a half years of lease income to remain unrecovered.

The Auditor General reported that 2 acres and 15.18 perches of Pembruk Estate in Kalutara District had been leased to Vintor Fashions (Private) Limited for 30 years from February 1992 to establish a garment factory. The company had defaulted on lease rent, with Rs. 2,661,282 in arrears up to February 2015, while 2016 and 2017 rent and surcharges had not yet been computed.

The Auditor General reported that 2 roods and 16 perches of Rathwetiya Estate, including a tea factory building, had been leased to the Sangaruwanketha Milk Producers' Cooperative Society Limited in May 1997 by deviating from the normal leasing procedure. No lease rent had been paid for about 15 years, arrears and surcharges had reached Rs. 4,596,800 by May 2016, and no action had been taken to cancel the lease agreement or otherwise enforce it.
